title: Unauthorized disclosure of continuous health telemetry
description: The wearable device continuously captures sensitive health data (heart rate, GPS position) which could be disclosed to unauthorized parties through device compromise, insecure transmission, or unauthorized data sharing.
assumptions: Assumes device may be vulnerable to attacks or data may be shared without explicit consent

title: Unauthorized access to device and captured data
description: The wearable device could be vulnerable to unauthorized access by attackers, potentially allowing them to access, modify, or exfiltrate the continuously captured sensor telemetry data.
assumptions: Assumes device may have security vulnerabilities or be connected to networks that could be compromised

title: Unintended consequences of continuous location tracking
description: Continuous GPS position tracking could have unintended consequences such as enabling surveillance, stalking, or creating detailed movement profiles without explicit user awareness or consent.
assumptions: Assumes continuous tracking may occur without user awareness or explicit consent for all tracking activities

title: User unawareness of data sharing
description: The user may not be aware that their calorie, meal, and weight data is being collected, stored, and potentially shared with third parties beyond their expectations.
assumptions: User may not fully understand the data lifecycle of their health information.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of health data
description: Sensitive health data (calories, meals, weight) could be disclosed to unauthorized parties during transmission or storage in the companion app.
assumptions: Data transmission and storage mechanisms may not be adequately secured.

title: Data loss during user input transmission
description: User-entered data (calories, meals, weight) may be lost during transmission from the user's device to the companion app or during storage.
assumptions: Network transmission and local storage may not be fully reliable.

title: Unnecessary Health Data Collection
description: The companion mobile app may collect and store more health data than strictly necessary for the intended purpose, violating the minimality principle. Calorie intake, weight history, and exercise sessions may include granular details that exceed what is required for basic health tracking.
assumptions: Assumes the app collects all specified health log types without user consent or necessity assessment.

title: Implicit Data Disclosure Through Metadata
description: Health logs written to the data store may contain implicit metadata or derived information that discloses personal data without explicit user awareness. For example, timestamps, frequency of entries, or patterns in exercise sessions could reveal sensitive behavioral information.
assumptions: Assumes data store may retain or expose metadata alongside health log content.

title: Third-Party Data Sharing Without Consent
description: Health logs written to the data store may be shared with third parties (e.g., fitness partners, insurance providers, advertisers) without explicit user consent or knowledge, representing an unintended data disclosure.
assumptions: Assumes the data store or app may have integrations with external services.

title: Data Store Access by Unauthorized Parties
description: The health log store may be accessible to unauthorized parties through misconfigured access controls, API endpoints, or data breaches, leading to unintended disclosure of sensitive health information.
assumptions: Assumes the data store has some form of access control that may be misconfigured or bypassed.

title: Data Retention Beyond Necessity
description: The health log store may retain health data beyond what is strictly required for the intended purpose, increasing the risk of future data breaches and violating data minimization principles.
assumptions: Assumes the data store has retention policies that may exceed necessary timeframes.

title: Explicit Location Data Disclosure
description: GPS location traces are intentionally written to the location history store, which may be accessed by third parties or used for profiling beyond the intended purpose.

title: Implicit Location Data Disclosure
description: Location data stored in DS2 may be indirectly disclosed to third parties through data sharing, API integrations, or secondary use without explicit user consent.

title: Location Data Information Leakage
description: GPS location traces stored in DS2 may be exposed to unauthorized parties through data store access, backup, or export mechanisms.

title: Location Data Integrity Compromise
description: GPS location traces stored in DS2 may be corrupted, altered, or tampered with, affecting the accuracy and reliability of location history.

title: Unintended Location Data Disclosure
description: Location data may be inadvertently shared with unauthorized parties through data store access, API integrations, or data processing activities.

title: Unintended Data Disclosure to Third Parties
description: Personal health data (calorie, weight, exercise logs) stored in DS1 may be disclosed to third parties through the analytics service P3, either intentionally (e.g., sharing with healthcare providers) or unintentionally (e.g., data leakage, unauthorized access). The minimality principle may not be followed, collecting more data than strictly required for health-condition analysis.

title: Explicit Data Disclosure for Health Analysis
description: The analytics service P3 explicitly reads personal health data from DS1 for health-condition analysis. While this is an intended disclosure, it may involve more data than strictly necessary, potentially violating the minimality principle in data collection and processing.

title: Implicit Data Disclosure Through Analytics
description: The analytics service P3 may inadvertently disclose personal health data through derived insights, metadata, or secondary uses of the health-condition analysis, creating implicit disclosures that were not explicitly intended.

title: Information Leakage Through Access Logs
description: Access to health data in DS1 by P3 may generate access logs that could reveal sensitive information about which users accessed what data, potentially leading to information leakage about user behavior patterns.

title: Unintended Data Sharing with External Parties
description: The analytics service P3 may share health data with external parties (e.g., researchers, insurance companies, employers) without explicit consent or proper authorization, creating unintended data disclosures.

title: Profiling of health condition groups through inferred insights
description: Health Analytics Service infers health-condition risk indicators, routine summaries, and trend flags that may profile individuals and transfer knowledge to other individuals through known relations of group membership or similarity.
assumptions: Assumes the analytics service has access to individual health data that can be used to generate group-level insights.

title: Insufficient cybersecurity risk management for health data transmission
description: Health Analytics Service may transmit inferred health insights to Companion Mobile App without adequate cybersecurity risk management measures, creating privacy risks through potential interception or unauthorized access during data transfer.
assumptions: Assumes the data flow between P3 and P2 occurs over a network and may be vulnerable to interception.

title: Unauthorized disclosure of sensitive health indicators
description: The app dashboard displays inferred eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals to the user. If the user lacks proper consent or if the data is displayed without appropriate safeguards, this could constitute unauthorized disclosure of sensitive health information.

title: Identification of user health status through inferred indicators
description: The app displays inferred condition indicators that can identify the user's health status (eating-disorder or diabetes risk). This could lead to identification of the user's sensitive health information through the dashboard display.

title: User unawareness of data display and implications
description: The user may be unaware of what health-related data is being displayed on the dashboard or how it is being used. This lack of awareness could lead to inappropriate use of the displayed information.

title: Non-compliance with health data protection regulations
description: Displaying sensitive health indicators (eating-disorder or diabetes risk signals) may not comply with applicable health data protection regulations (e.g., GDPR, HIPAA). This could lead to legal and organizational risk.

title: Unnecessary transfer of health and location data to third-party cloud provider
description: The Health Analytics Service transfers full health and location datasets to the Cloud Hosting Provider. This explicit disclosure of personal data to a third party may violate the minimality principle if the data is not strictly required for the intended purpose. The transfer of complete datasets rather than only necessary subsets increases privacy risk.
assumptions: The cloud provider is a third party outside the system boundary and may have different security and privacy standards.

title: Potential information leakage during data transfer to cloud provider
description: During the transfer of analytics data, models, and health/location datasets to the Cloud Hosting Provider, there is a risk of data interception, unauthorized access, or leakage during transmission. This could expose sensitive personal information to unauthorized parties.
assumptions: The transfer occurs over a network and may be subject to interception or unauthorized access.

title: Unintended disclosure through metadata or derived data
description: The transfer of health and location datasets to the cloud provider may result in unintended disclosures through metadata, derived information, or incidental data that could be used to infer sensitive personal information beyond the explicitly disclosed data.
assumptions: Metadata and derived data from the transferred datasets may contain additional personal information.
